## 2026-05-02 — Initial a11y plan generated by `/andromeda-a11y`
**Section:** §1 Scope, §3 Harness Contract, §6 Visual Verification, §9 CI, §11 Anti-Patterns — every tool pick, version, and the tier decision below is current truth in those sections; only the selection *rationale* is history kept here.
**Change:** First generation of the plan. A11y tier Standard (1) → WCAG 2.1 AA (~50 SCs) with a motion-sensitive AAA escalation (SC 2.3.3 Animation from Interactions). Tool stack:
- A11y testing: `@axe-core/playwright` 4.11.x + Lighthouse 12.x + pa11y 9.x
- Focus management: focus-trap-react 12.x + tabbable 6.4.x
- ARIA components: React Aria Components 1.17.x OR Headless UI 2.2.x (never both)
- Motion / reduced-motion: Tailwind v4 `motion-reduce:` / `motion-safe:` variants + `motion/react` 12.x `useReducedMotion`
- Contrast: axe-core color-contrast rule + colorjs.io 0.6.x token-based checker
**Why:** axe-core covers ~50 WCAG 2.1 AA SCs via tagged rules and piggybacks on the tests' Playwright 5-command E2E harness; Lighthouse 12 adds the prefers-reduced-motion (SC 2.3.3 AAA) + focus-visible (SC 2.4.7) audits; pa11y 9 gives a parallel rule matrix. focus-trap-react handles modal entry/exit/escape-close/focus-restore (SC 2.1.2 / SC 2.4.3); tabbable computes the expected Tab order for assertions. React Aria covers the Dialog / RadioGroup / Slider / Switch / ComboBox / Menu / Tabs / Form patterns of P2–P7 (Headless UI is lighter for Tailwind-tight builds); never mix the two. colorjs.io implements the WCAG 2.1 contrast algorithm and reads design tokens verbatim via `getComputedStyle`. Tier justified by 2 primary UI surfaces (desktop-webview + desktop-native tray), 8 assertable entities, 7 must-be-accessible flows (P1–P7), tests + obs both Standard, security Minimal (no regulated-compliance trigger). No open questions deferred.
